OK.

I would recommend to have everything left aligned, and do not enforce a length of 64 bits. This way it will be easy to add another identity needing more bits in the future if required.

Option values are zero-padded to 32-bit boundaries. From there I thought that storing everything greater than 32-bit and lower than 64 as a uint64 would make it easier to write parser and serializer. I see your point thought, let's keep everything left aligned and with its proper bit length.

Thanks. Does it make sense to reuse the subtree definition across the different identifiers? Normally no more than one xCGI should appear in a packet. What do you think?
I'm fine with a single tree item
Ok
You have a mix of decimal and hexadecimal, which is not coherent

I used hexadecimal for NCI and ECI to make it easier for users to recognize the two components (node and cell ID). Furthermore, sometimes operators use the hexadecimal notation because it makes it easy to spot a common binary prefix (e.g. 0x21xxxxx eNodeBs are the ones of a particular supplier).
If it looks incoherent I will switch everything to decimal.

The 3G cell identity, LAC and the cell global identifier are displayed as decimal, while the rest is displayed as hexadecimal which does not seem homogeneous (you highlight the fact that the hex syntax can be useful but display the cell global identifier as decimal which is unusable).
Maybe always display the cell global identifier as BASE_HEX, and use BASE_HEX_DEC for the others?
Thanks. I hope I got it right.
